results.title: Authentication
results.snippet:
Create and manage API credentials in [Higgsfield Console](https://console.higgsfield.ai). Each credential consists of a key ID and a secret. Send both values in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET
```
```
curl https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/status \
--header "Authorization: Key ${HF_API_KEY_ID}:${HF_API_KEY_SECRET}"
```
The API also accepts the legacy `hf-api-key` and `hf-secret` headers. New integrations should use the `Authorization` header.
##
​
Keep credentials server-side
Do not call the API directly from browser or mobile application code. Anyone who can inspect the application can extract its API secret and use your account.
- Store credentials in a secrets manager or encrypted environment variables.
- Use separate credentials for development and production.
- Never include credentials in URLs, logs, screenshots, or support messages.
- Rotate a credential immediately if it may have been exposed.
##
​
Authentication errors
Missing, malformed, or invalid credentials return `401 Unauthorized`:
```
{
"detail": "Invalid credentials"
}
```

results.title: Higgsfield MCP Moves to CIMD: What Developers Need to Know
results.snippet:
Higgsfield MCP is moving client identification from Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) to Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD). DCR is switched off on January 1, 2027, and CIMD becomes the only way for a third-party client to identify itself. Developers whose MCP client registers through DCR must migrate before that date.

Both methods work now. Only the way a client identifies itself to `https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp` changes. The rest of the OAuth flow stays the same.

With DCR, a client sends a registration request, and the authorization server issues a `client_id` and stores it. With CIMD, the `client_id` is an HTTPS URL that the developer controls, and the authorization server reads the client metadata from that URL.
How Is CIMD Different From DCR?
| Criteria | DCR | CIMD |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | Opaque string issued by the server | HTTPS URL of the metadata document |
| Registration request | Required for every installation | None |
| Where metadata lives | On the authorization server | On the developer's domain |
| Updating metadata | Re-register | Edit the document |
| Identity | Unverified, anyone can register any name | Tied to a domain the developer controls |

results.title: Meet the Higgsfield API: How It Works and What You Get
results.snippet:
The Higgsfield API is a self-serve API for developers that provides direct access to more than 50 current video and image generation models with pay-as-you-go billing in US dollars. There is no subscription: you top up a balance, pay per generation at published rates, and spending stops automatically at zero.

The Higgsfield API gives developers programmatic access to a curated catalog of video and image generation models. If you are building a product that generates video or images, you normally assemble model access from several providers, each with its own billing logic, expiration rules, and rate structures. Estimating what a month of production traffic will cost becomes a separate task. The Higgsfield API is built around a different setup: one key, one balance in US dollars, and a public price list, so you can calculate your costs on your own volume before you commit to anything.
The API is a separate product from the [higgsfield.ai](http://higgsfield.ai) website. A plan on [higgsfield.ai](http://higgsfield.ai) does not affect API access, and API usage is billed independently.

Setting up access takes four steps:
1. Create an account and choose between personal and company use

results.title: What is the Higgsfield API, and how do I get started?
results.snippet:
A subscription on [higgsfield.ai](http://higgsfield.ai) and the API are two separate products with separate billing. Your plan, credits, and Unlimited access exist only on the website; the API runs on its own account balance in US dollars.
How is the API different from my Higgsfield plan?
| Criteria | Higgsfield plan ([higgsfield.ai](https://higgsfield.ai/)) | Higgsfield API |
|---|---|---|
| Who it's for | Creators working in the visual interface | Developers building generation into their own products |
| Billing | Subscription plus credits | US dollar balance, pay per generation |
| Unlimited models | Yes, where included in plan | Not applicable |
| Requires the other | No | No |

Billing is pay-as-you-go from a US dollar balance, and the minimum top-up is $5. Video models are priced per second of output and image models per image; DoP is the exception, priced per generation. Each model has a fixed rate for every configuration: the rate depends on settings like resolution and audio, is listed publicly, and stays the same regardless of how much you top up. |---|---|
| Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop) | Custom connector with the MCP server URL |
| ChatGPT | Official Higgsfield Plugin from the Plugins Directory |

| Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes | Higgsfield CLI, set up by the agent itself |

## What is Higgsfield MCP?
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open protocol that lets AI agents connect to external services and call their tools. Higgsfield MCP is a connector that lets you generate images, videos, characters, and audio from Higgsfield directly inside Claude or another MCP-compatible agent. It isn't the Higgsfield API: MCP connects to your existing account and uses your existing plan credits, with no API key required. For building generation into your own product with per-request billing, see [What is the Higgsfield API, and how do I get started?](https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/integrations/what-is-the-higgsfield-api)
